title: Computational identification and characterization of high-risk human KRAS nsSNPs: Impacting structure, ligand binding, and cancer prognosis.
authors: Hossain, Md Mainuddin; Adhikari, Juthi; Ahmed, Sabbir; Zaki, Md Zakiul Islam; Khandaker, Afia; Shibly, Abu Zaffar
one_liner_zh: 该文通过计算工具预测KRAS nsSNP的致病性，并结合分子对接和MD模拟评估突变对蛋白结构、配体结合及癌症预后的影响，属于蛋白质结构相关的计算研究，但方法以现有工具应用为主，创新性一般。
abstract: Kristen rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) is a critical oncogene regulating cell proliferation and survival, with mutations driving tumorigenesis. Non-synonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms (nsSNPs) can alter KRAS structure, function, and ligand interactions, influencing clinical outcomes. This study analyzed 324 nsSNPs from dbSNP, ClinVar, and DisGeNET using eight predictive tools (SIFT, PolyPhen-2, PredictSNP, PhD-SNP, PANTHER, PROVEAN, Meta-SNP, SNAP2) to identify highly deleterious nsSNPs. Protein stability was evaluated via I-Mutant 2.0, MUpro, INPS-MD, iStable, and DDMut, and structural impacts assessed using HOPE, MutPred2, and Missense3D. Molecular docking (AutoDock Vina) and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations explored ligand-specific interactions. Cancer susceptibilities analysis was performed using CScape, Dr. Cancer, and FATHMM. Our analysis consistently predicted sixteen nsSNPs as highly deleterious, with Y71D and M72K identified as high-risk variants located in the GTP-binding domain, destabilizing KRAS and disrupting hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions. Docking and simulation analyses showed that the Y71D and M72K nsSNPs reduced binding affinity and stability with ligand sotorasib (CID: 137278711) compared to wild-type KRAS, whereas both high-risk nsSNPs exhibited enhanced binding and stability with ligand adagrasib (CID: 138611145), indicating mutation-dependent ligand interactions. MM-GBSA analysis confirmed mutation-dependent KRAS binding changes, weakening sotorasib affinity while enhancing adagrasib interaction in the Y71D variant. Cancer susceptibilities analyses indicated both Y71D and M72K may promote cancer prognosis. These results highlight Y71D and M72K as high-risk KRAS nsSNPs affecting structural stability, ligand interactions, and cancer prognosis, providing a framework for mutation-specific therapeutic strategies and supporting further experimental validation in precision oncology.
abstract_zh: Kristen大鼠肉瘤病毒癌基因同源物（KRAS）是调控细胞增殖和存活的关键癌基因，其突变驱动肿瘤发生。非同义单核苷酸多态性（nsSNPs）可改变KRAS的结构、功能和配体相互作用，从而影响临床结局。本研究利用八种预测工具（SIFT、PolyPhen-2、PredictSNP、PhD-SNP、PANTHER、PROVEAN、Meta-SNP、SNAP2）分析了来自dbSNP、ClinVar和DisGeNET的324个nsSNPs，以识别高度有害的nsSNPs。通过I-Mutant 2.0、MUpro、INPS-MD、iStable和DDMut评估蛋白质稳定性，并使用HOPE、MutPred2和Missense3D评估结构影响。分子对接（AutoDock Vina）和100纳秒分子动力学模拟探索了配体特异性相互作用。癌症易感性分析使用CScape、Dr. Cancer和FATHMM进行。我们的分析一致预测十六个nsSNPs为高度有害，其中Y71D和M72K被鉴定为位于GTP结合域的高风险变异，使KRAS不稳定并破坏疏水性和静电相互作用。对接和模拟分析表明，与野生型KRAS相比，Y71D和M72K nsSNPs降低了与配体sotorasib（CID: 137278711）的结合亲和力和稳定性，而两种高风险nsSNPs均表现出与配体adagrasib（CID: 138611145）增强的结合和稳定性，表明突变依赖性配体相互作用。MM-GBSA分析证实了突变依赖性KRAS结合变化，在Y71D变异中削弱了sotorasib亲和力，同时增强了adagrasib相互作用。癌症易感性分析表明，Y71D和M72K均可能促进癌症预后。这些结果突出表明Y71D和M72K是影响结构稳定性、配体相互作用和癌症预后的高风险KRAS nsSNPs，为突变特异性治疗策略提供了框架，并支持精准肿瘤学中的进一步实验验证。
